thread:
maya: quick check — I'm wiring up a Java embedding+rerank flow using the client batch helper and hitting a dim mismatch at the reranker stage. batcher outputs 1536-d vectors but the rerank model expects 1024. not sure where the down-conversion should happen, or if i'm accidentally concatenating extras. any tips?

kevin: are you using quantized checkpoints or a different model for rerank? dims can differ across model variants. which models in the pipeline?

maya: pipeline is `text-embed-large-v2` for embeddings -> `rerank-mini-1024` for scoring. embed client config is pretty basic: 
```java
EmbedClient.Builder b = new EmbedClient.Builder()
  .batchSize(64)
  .padTo(256) // padding on inputs
  .model("text-embed-large-v2")
  .auth(token)
  .enableStreaming(false);
```
Then i run the batcher and hand outputs into rerank scorer. logs show vector length 1536.

tom: two quick things: 1) tokenization/pooling mismatch (some embed models return pooled vectors with extra dims if you enable `append_hidden`-style flags), 2) check the client post-process pipeline — are you doing concat of token & pooled outputs?

olivia: also, in Java SDK there was a recent change to default to `enable_metadata=true` which added a trailing 512-d metadata vector for a while. if you updated SDK versions that might explain 1536 (1024 + 512). what version of the SDK are you on?

maya: ahhh i'm on `redwood-java-sdk 1.4.0` — we bumped last week. i can try 1.3.2. good catch.

kevin: if downgrade isn't ideal, we should add a compatibility helper: `EmbedBatcher.normalizeDims(vecs, targetDim)` that will error early or do a safe projection. i can PR a small util.

maya: that would be great. another unrelated weirdness — when I enable client-side streaming for long batches i sometimes get truncated streams when a retry happens after a 401. the retry seems to start a second stream and client code ends up taking the first partial chunk. anyone seen streaming+auth race?

olivia: yes — there was a race with token refresh. Current behavior: 401 triggers automatic refresh + retry, but the streaming reader doesn't clear partial buffers unless you explicitly close and re-open. Workaround: in the streaming callback check for `onError` with status 401 and then drop buffer and re-init. We're planning to make the client auto-reset the stream on auth retry.

tom: short-term: set `authRetry=false` on the streaming options and handle refresh manually. Also log the `request_id` and server `attempt` header so SRE can correlate duplicate streams.

maya: thanks — will try disabling authRetry for streaming. kevin: if you PR the dim-normalize helper, can you also add a small warning in the Java release notes about the metadata default? will save others.

kevin: yup, i'll open the PR and a one-liner in the changelog.

embed-bot: CI: java-sdk-integration-tests failed on `embed-batcher-normalize` job (job id 4342). see https://ci.redwood.com/build/4342 for logs.

olivia: filing a quick internal ticket to track the metadata change and add an opt-out flag: INF-972. tagging @engineering-release.

maya: one last nit — pagination: i'm using the batch helper to paginate a huge corpus. is it better to page on the client side with a cursor or call the server with offsets? performance-wise what's recommended?

kevin: prefer cursor/prefix-based pagination with the batch helper. offsets can be expensive for very large corpuses, and cursoring lets you resume after a partial run. make sure to persist the last cursor and save a small checkpoint after each successful batch write.

tom: also remember to set `maxConcurrentBatches` to limit memory if you have streaming enabled — otherwise you can OOM with too many in-flight streams.

maya: awesome, thanks everyone. i'll try 1) confirm SDK downgrade vs helper, 2) disable authRetry for streaming and add manual refresh handler, 3) switch to cursor pagination for large jobs. i'll post back with the failing log snippets if anything persists. :raised_hands:
